after.description_1: Schipholparkeren is built around one urgent visitor task: reserving secure parking close to Schiphol. The website needed to make arrival and return dates, parking choices and practical extras easy to understand before travellers commit to a reservation.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress journey around the booking flow, with clear choices for valet and comfort parking and supporting services such as charging, washing and refuelling. Safety, transparent pricing and FAQs support the decision while repeated reservation actions keep the next step obvious on desktop and mobile.

before.description_1: Casareno needed sharper page content because the offer, process, and next step were not always clear to visitors. The old structure made the website feel less direct, which created friction before contact.
before.description_2: I redesigned the content flow with clearer English copy, stronger section order, better visual hierarchy, and a smoother path to contact. The result is a calmer website that explains the consultancy offer more quickly.

after.description_1: Casareno focuses on construction, renovation and maintenance, from turn-key projects and new-build work to bathrooms, floors, stairs, doors, frames and finishing. The website needed to communicate that range while giving prospective clients enough project evidence and process detail to trust the company before requesting advice.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around services, completed projects and Casareno’s five-step working process. Visitors can move from a specific renovation or building need into relevant project examples, understand the route from introduction to delivery and then book a free advice conversation without losing context.

before.description_1: Pastrycompany had useful webshop information, but the message needed a calmer structure and clearer priority. Visitors needed to scan the page, understand the practical value, and see a simple route forward. The content also had to sound specific instead of broad or interchangeable. It made the next step clearer sooner.
before.description_2: I rewrote the content and organised the page so each section answers a clear visitor question. The result explains the webshop work in plain English, connects benefits to real decisions, and keeps contact options close. This makes the case easier to read, compare, and trust. It made choices easier too.

after.description_1: Pastrycompany combines an online food shop with catering and event services. The website therefore needed to support quick product ordering while also giving customers enough information to consider larger catering or event requests.
after.description_2: I organised the WooCommerce experience so product categories, offers and ordering stay easy to use, while catering, event services, reviews, location information and contact form a separate but connected route. This lets visitors switch naturally between buying products and planning a larger occasion.

before.description_1: Ourwp needed the website to answer practical visitor questions faster. The business offer had to be described with clear context, useful detail, and a visible path to contact. Without a tighter structure, the page risked feeling generic and harder to judge on smaller screens. It supported faster decisions before contact.
before.description_2: I refined the page by reducing repetition, improving the order of information, and making each section easier to scan. The WordPress build presents the business offer with practical context and steady pacing. Visitors get clearer reasons to continue, compare the work, and start a conversation. It made choices easier too.

after.description_1: OurWP provides virtual-office and business-address services for entrepreneurs, including a KvK registration address, post handling and scanning options. The website needed to explain these practical services and packages clearly because visitors are often comparing addresses, pricing and registration requirements before signing up.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress journey around the main business-address proposition, package comparison and common practical questions. Clear signup, contact and account routes help visitors move from understanding the service to registering, while post-handling information remains easy to find throughout the site.

before.description_1: The beauty-webshop page for Byderma needed to remove hesitation before inquiry. Visitors were likely comparing providers, so the page had to explain the work quickly, show relevant details, and keep the next step obvious. Long, general wording would have made the offer feel less certain. It made choices easier too.
before.description_2: I created a more direct page flow with concise headings, specific project wording, and WordPress content fields that stay easy to maintain. The design gives Byderma a clearer presentation, while visitors can scan the work, understand the value, and move toward contact without confusion. It supported faster decisions before contact.

after.description_1: ByDerma combines beauty treatments with a large WooCommerce product catalogue, appointments and member benefits. The main challenge was to keep treatment discovery, shopping and booking distinct enough to understand while still feeling like one consistent beauty platform.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress and WooCommerce experience around those separate tasks. Treatment information leads naturally to appointment booking, the webshop keeps product discovery and purchasing focused, and supporting account or membership content remains accessible without interrupting either journey. The same hierarchy stays clear on mobile.

before.description_1: MDV Installaties needed a clearer installation page because visitors had to understand the offer before making contact. The existing story needed stronger order, more specific wording, and fewer general lines. People comparing options needed quick context, visible next steps, and enough practical detail to decide whether to continue. It mattered.
before.description_2: I rebuilt the page around clearer sections, direct English copy, and practical WordPress content blocks. The structure shows what the work involves, why it matters, and how visitors can respond. Stronger scanning, calmer wording, and focused contact routes help people compare the project and make decisions with confidence. It mattered.

after.description_1: MDV Installaties brings electrical work, renovations, service and maintenance and locksmith support together in one business website. The structure needed to distinguish planned installation projects from service requests so visitors could identify the right help quickly.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress content into clear service routes with practical explanations and direct contact points. Electrical work, renovation, maintenance and locksmith services each get enough context to stand on their own, while the responsive layout keeps urgent and planned enquiries easy to reach on smaller screens.

before.description_1: C&K Bouw needed a website that answers practical visitor questions faster. The construction services had to be explained with clear context, useful detail and an easy route to contact. Without a tighter structure, the page risked feeling too generic and harder to judge on smaller screens.
before.description_2: I refined the page by reducing repetition, improving the order of information and making each section easier to scan. The WordPress build presents the construction services with practical context and a steady flow, giving visitors clearer reasons to compare the work and start a conversation.

after.description_1: C&K Bouw serves more than one audience: clients looking for construction support, employers needing professionals and people looking for work. The website needed to keep project capability and recruitment information separate so each visitor could reach the right content without sorting through the other journey.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress site around audience-specific routes for construction services, vacancies and staffing. Shared brand and trust content connects the experience, while clear enquiry and application actions help clients, candidates and employers move forward from the relevant section.

before.description_1: Before the update, Proline Afbouw needed sharper page content because important finishing details were not always clear at first glance. Visitors needed a stronger introduction, better section flow, and wording that explained the offer in normal language before they committed to contacting the business. It supported faster decisions before contact.
before.description_2: I gave Proline Afbouw a clearer structure with sharper English copy, logical content blocks, and a smoother route from introduction to contact. The page explains the finishing work without extra noise, helps visitors compare faster, and keeps the WordPress presentation consistent across screen sizes. It supported faster decisions before contact.

after.description_1: Proline Afbouw offers specialist finishing services including latex spraying, system ceilings and walls, metal-stud work, plastering and painting. The website needed to separate these services clearly and give prospective customers enough project and review context before they request a quotation.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress experience around dedicated service areas, supporting project examples and reviews. Clear quotation and contact routes stay close to the relevant finishing information, making the broad offer easier to scan and compare on desktop and mobile.

before.description_1: Connectwerk needed sharper content, so visitors could quickly understand what the recruitment service offers. The page needed readable sections, specific wording and enough context to build trust, while keeping the first contact step simple and low-pressure.
before.description_2: I built the final page around plain language, balanced sections and contact moments that appear once visitors have enough context. The recruitment message now feels more natural and practical, giving Connectwerk a stronger portfolio case and visitors a clearer path forward.

after.description_1: Connectwerk serves both candidates looking for vacancies and employers looking for staffing support. The website needed to separate those two journeys while still using shared sector expertise to explain what Connectwerk does and where it adds value.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience so vacancy browsing and candidate registration form one clear route, while employer information and staffing enquiries form another. Sector-focused content supports both audiences without mixing their primary actions, keeping applications and business enquiries easier to complete.
